maya: quick question: who ultimately owns batching/caching/quantization choices across hosted/dedicated/private? intent vs enforcement?
simon: intent = API (latency/cost enum). enforcement = control-plane + runtime. control-plane chooses profiles, runtime applies.
lin: add: dedicated tenants must opt-in for changes. private installs can run in local-control mode and ignore control-plane.
caro: runtime should advertise capabilities on handshake: max_batch, kv_layout, supported_variants. control-plane uses that to select safe profiles.
maya: how do we handle runtime rejections?
simon: standard rejection codes: INCOMPATIBLE, AUTHZ_DENIED, CIRCUIT_OPEN. control-plane must fallback or surface audit.
ops-bot: note: emit audit events on policy.apply / policy.reject with actor, policy_id, reason, trace_id. redact before leaving customer VPC.
lin: public API: keep enums (LOW/MED/HIGH). enterprise header allowed for numeric SLA.
maya: action items: maya RFC for ownership matrix; simon handshake proto; caro telemetry schema; lin test harness. thanks.
